summary: Unpredictable single insert performance due to potential blocking and excessive indexing.
symptoms: Single record insert takes an unusually long time (e.g., 7 minutes).
Blocking sessions reported in sys.dm_exec_requests but the blocker session is not active.
Wait type observed as LCK_M_S during blocking.
mechanism: Blocking caused by uncommitted transactions or excessive index maintenance during inserts.

facts.evidence: The table is described as having 8 million rows.
The table has 34 indexes in addition to a clustered index.
The wait type observed during blocking is LCK_M_S.
The blocking session is reported in sys.dm_exec_requests but is not active in sys.dm_exec_sessions.

assumptions: The blocking is caused by uncommitted transactions holding locks.
The high number of indexes contributes to the poor insert performance.
The database environment supports SQL Server-compatible locking and indexing mechanisms.
unknowns: The exact workload pattern causing the blocking.
Whether the blocking session is due to a specific application behavior or a system issue.
The impact of the 34 indexes on insert performance in this specific scenario.
